_note: Machine-readable NEXUS scenario contracts. Each runbook declares the governing object, explicit non-object, accountable decision owner, mandatory decision/evidence artifacts, termination criteria, and an installable roster. The Strategic Assurance Lead is mandatory in every material runbook. Agent entries are filename-stem slugs and must resolve to catalog agents. Strategy documentation constrains orchestration; it does not grant real-world execution authority.

runbooks.title: Strategic Decision & Transition
runbooks.summary: Frame a material decision from superior purpose through actor geometry, causal logic, reaction, concentration, evidence, and transition, with independent challenge before irreversible commitment.
runbooks.governing_object: Produce a decision-ready strategic choice whose superior purpose, causal mechanism, authority, resource concentration, alternatives, refutators, reactions, and transition conditions are explicit enough for an accountable human owner to decide.
runbooks.non_object: Generate strategy theater, maximize analysis volume, manufacture consensus, or convert an agent recommendation into execution authority.
runbooks.decision_owner: Named human or institutional authority accountable for the material decision
runbooks.termination_criteria: Close the strategic decision cycle when the authorized owner records a bounded decision and review/termination conditions, or terminate/redesign when a fatal authority, admissibility, causal, evidence, or conservation defect remains unresolved.

roster.activation: as required by the decision geometry
only after an authorized bounded decision

runbooks.title: Startup MVP Build
runbooks.summary: Test a bounded product thesis and ship the smallest evidence-generating product without confusing feature delivery with product-market validation.
runbooks.governing_object: Establish whether a specific customer problem can be solved by a usable, supportable product strongly enough to justify the next material investment.
runbooks.non_object: Maximize feature count, sprint velocity, launch speed, or demo polish as ends in themselves.
runbooks.termination_criteria: Close, redesign, or narrow the initiative when the declared falsifier is met, required authority/resources cannot be obtained, or the minimum sufficient result is achieved and transferred to ordinary ownership.

roster.activation: when permitted by the current strategic output
only after the relevant value and audience hypothesis is testable

runbooks.title: Enterprise Feature Development
runbooks.summary: Deliver a material enterprise capability without sacrificing system integrity, compliance, maintainability, or stakeholder authority for roadmap completion.
runbooks.governing_object: Produce a validated enterprise capability that improves the declared user/business outcome while remaining compatible with the existing product, controls, and operating model.
runbooks.non_object: Ship the roadmap item, maximize scope, or satisfy a single stakeholder metric regardless of system-level consequences.
runbooks.decision_owner: Authorized product/program owner with relevant security/compliance concurrence
runbooks.termination_criteria: Stop or redesign when a fatal security/compliance/architecture condition emerges, the causal benefit thesis is falsified, or the validated capability is transferred to normal product and operations ownership.

roster.activation: when permitted by the current strategic output
as required by scope and before the relevant commitment
as needed and at material gates

runbooks.title: Strategy-Led Marketing Campaign
runbooks.summary: Diagnose the demand constraint before selecting channels, then activate only interventions whose causal role, evidence plan, resources, reactions, and stopping rules are explicit.
runbooks.governing_object: Improve a defined superior commercial or behavioral outcome by diagnosing the binding demand constraint and selecting the smallest coherent set of marketing interventions capable of changing it.
runbooks.non_object: Maximize impressions, posting frequency, engagement, follower growth, channel coverage, or campaign activity as ends in themselves.
runbooks.termination_criteria: Stop, reallocate, redesign, or re-diagnose when the demand/causal hypothesis is falsified, marginal effort no longer contributes to the governing object, a hard constraint is breached, or the sufficient result is reached and conserved.

roster.activation: only after diagnosis selects the relevant mechanism
only when selected by the strategic thesis

runbooks.title: Incident Response
runbooks.duration: incident-dependent; minutes to hours for containment, longer for conservation
runbooks.summary: Restore critical service safely, preserve evidence, and prevent recurrence without optimizing MTTR at the expense of integrity or learning.
runbooks.governing_object: Return the affected service to a safe, supportable condition while preserving evidence, controlling blast radius, and establishing the changes needed to prevent recurrence.
runbooks.non_object: Minimize MTTR, close the incident, or restore green dashboards regardless of residual risk, evidence loss, or recurrence.
runbooks.decision_owner: Named incident authority under the organization's incident policy
runbooks.termination_criteria: End emergency mode only when containment and recovery criteria are met, residual risks have owners, temporary authority/access is expired or transferred, and conservation actions are assigned to ordinary ownership.

roster.activation: according to the incident authority and affected system

runbooks.title: HTP Gate 0 — Solana + Arbitrum
runbooks.summary: Close an evidence-first, non-executing Gate 0 for bounded Solana and Arbitrum One DeFi risk-monitoring workstreams with chain-specific engineering, security, research, and legal review.
runbooks.governing_object: Determine whether a bounded, defensive Solana + Arbitrum One monitoring MVP is coherent, supportable, legally reviewable, and falsifiable before any live-service or executing capability is authorized.
runbooks.non_object: Maximize chain coverage, MEV capture, exploitability knowledge, detector count, or speed to live execution.
runbooks.decision_owner: HTP Governance or explicitly delegated Gate 0 owner
runbooks.termination_criteria: Gate 0 closes with PROCEED, PROCEED_WITH_CONDITIONS, REDESIGN, or REJECT once the bounded artifacts and evidence are sufficient; HOLD persists only while a named evidence/authority condition remains unresolved. No Gate 0 result authorizes live offensive or executing capability.

roster.activation: domain map, technical reconciliation, and S1 handoff
jurisdiction/activity memo and before any live-service expansion

runbooks.title: The Marketing Mispricing Diagnostic
runbooks.summary: Separate demand creation from demand extraction in two weeks: classify marketing capital by job, run nine evidence-graded modules, challenge the thesis, and deliver a board-safe Mispricing Report and Repricing Memo.
runbooks.governing_object: Determine where a company's marketing capital is creating future demand and where it is harvesting demand that earlier brand investment already built, and state the reallocation that follows, with every material claim graded by evidence.
runbooks.non_object: Judge creative taste, audit agency performance, redesign the brand, or produce a growth forecast the evidence does not fund.
runbooks.decision_owner: Engagement lead, or the client-side CMO/CFO sponsor named in the Strategic Decision Record
runbooks.termination_criteria: The diagnostic closes when the Availability Ledger, the nine modules, and the Repricing Memo are delivered with every material claim graded [FACT]/[INFERENCE]/[HYPOTHESIS]/[JUDGMENT] and every gap named. It terminates early, with findings stated as incomplete, if budget, spend or measurement data sufficient to separate creation from extraction cannot be obtained. No output authorizes a reallocation the client's own governance has not approved.

termination_contract.achieved: The Availability Ledger classifies the period's marketing capital by job, the nine modules are graded, and the Repricing Memo states the reallocation the evidence supports.
termination_contract.outstanding: Every module the data could not close is listed by name with the data that would close it — not omitted and not softened into a judgement.
termination_contract.accountable: The client-side sponsor named in the Strategic Decision Record owns the reallocation after handover; the engagement lead owns the findings and their evidence grades.
termination_contract.on_breach: If the client presents a graded claim at a higher status than the register records, or attributes a reallocation to this work that the memo does not support, the engagement lead corrects the record in writing and the diagnostic is not cited as its basis.
termination_contract.conservation_resources: A named owner for the Ratio Covenant and quarterly access to spend and measurement data; without both, the reallocation decays back to the prior split.
termination_contract.revision_conditions: Revisit when the brand/activation split moves more than ten points, the measurement model changes, or a distinctive asset is retired or redesigned.

runbooks.title: BORING WINS Chapter Production
runbooks.summary: Take a BORING WINS chapter from draft to publication-ready: architecture, argument, verified evidence, cross-work consistency, and line edit in the book's voice.
runbooks.governing_object: Bring a BORING WINS chapter to publishable state: the argument holds, every figure and citation traces to a verified source, and the prose keeps the book's register.
runbooks.non_object: Soften the cultural critique, convert the book into a framework or how-to manual, or let a hypothesis harden into doctrine because it has survived several drafts.
runbooks.termination_criteria: A chapter closes when its claims are registered and sourced, its tensions with the rest of the manuscript are recorded or resolved, and the author accepts the draft. It stops short of that when a load-bearing citation cannot be verified: the claim is cut or demoted to [HYPOTHESIS] rather than shipped as fact.

termination_contract.achieved: The chapter's claims are registered and sourced, its tensions with the rest of the manuscript are recorded or resolved, and the author has accepted the draft.
termination_contract.outstanding: Claims demoted for want of a verifiable source stay in the register at their real status, with the source that would restore them.
termination_contract.accountable: The author. Editorial agents hold no authority over what ships.
termination_contract.on_breach: If a figure or citation is found unverifiable after acceptance, the claim is cut or demoted in the register and every downstream deliverable quoting it is corrected — the book, the framework, and any client material that inherited it.
termination_contract.conservation_resources: The proposition register outlives the chapter; it is the artifact that keeps the manuscript and the commercial layer telling the same story.
termination_contract.revision_conditions: Revisit when a cited source is superseded, when a chapter's argument changes upstream, or when the same claim appears at two different statuses in two documents.
